Without a jitter buffer, network packet arrival variation causes playback gaps or buffer underruns — streaming ceases to operate reliably. This passes the removal test: remove jitter buffer, streaming playback as designed breaks.

payload.note: An audio-packet is a network transmission unit that encapsulates audio frames with headers. It operates on audio-frame as its content substrate — remove audio-frame and the packet has no audio payload to transmit, ceasing to function as a container. The removal test passes constitutively.

Cepstral analysis operates on the cepstrum, which is derived from spectral analysis via FFT of the log power spectrum. Remove spectral analysis and cepstral analysis has no input data to process — the entire pipeline collapses.

Audio streaming operates by transmitting discrete audio frames over a network in sequence. Remove audio-frame and streaming has no unit of content to transmit — the temporal sequence of frames IS the stream. Removal test passes constitutively.

payload.reasoning: Packet's pinned sense is a transmission unit whose payload IS an audio frame; remove the frame and the unit has nothing to transmit - it degrades to a bare network packet. Removal test holds in the pinned sense (Law 11d), same operand-removal shape the court admitted for interleaving DEPENDS_ON sample.

The cepstrum is constructed from the log power spectrum via FFT - the input of cepstral analysis IS the output of spectral analysis. Remove spectral analysis and there is no spectrum left to process; the pipeline collapses at its source. Textbook removal test, present-tense necessity (Law 8b), not chronology.

In its carved real-time networked sense, streaming delivers discrete frames as its unit of content - the frame sequence is what gets scheduled, buffered and played. Remove audio-frame and streaming loses its unit of transmission; same operand-removal shape as interleaving DEPENDS_ON sample (Law 8b, pinned sense per Law 11d).

Removal test fails: streaming WITHOUT a jitter buffer still operates - over low-jitter networks, or degraded-but-continuous when it can't. The note itself only claims playback 'ceases to operate reliably' - degradation, not cessation (Law 8b requires stop-OPERATING). A jitter buffer is a mitigation against timing variation, not an operating prerequisite.
